summary: DirectionProvider and useDirection: tells every component which way the page reads, for Arabic, Hebrew and Persian.
figma: None — direction is a property of the page, not a component in the library

pairs.dont: Set dir="rtl" on the page and stop there.
pairs.do: Set dir on <html> and wrap the app in DirectionProvider with the same value.
pairs.why: CSS reads the attribute; Radix reads the provider. With only the attribute the layout mirrors and the keyboard does not, so the arrow that points at the next tab moves to the previous one.

pairs.dont: Wrap individual components in their own provider.
pairs.do: Provide direction once, at the root, beside the theme.
pairs.why: A page reads one way. A provider halfway down the tree means a portalled menu and the button that opened it can disagree.

pairs.dont: Call useDirection to choose between two classes.
pairs.do: Use a logical class (ps-, start-, border-s) or the rtl: variant, and keep the hook for geometry done in script.
pairs.why: A logical class costs nothing and cannot disagree with the DOM. The hook is for pointer maths, swipe direction and third-party props that take a direction.

pairs.dont: Let an IP address, a SIP trace, an ID or a metric take the page's direction.
pairs.do: Put ltr-island on the element that holds it.
pairs.why: Inside right-to-left text the bidi algorithm reorders punctuation: -5% reads as 5%- and 10.0.0.1:5060 comes apart at the colon.

pairs.dont: Mirror every icon and every picture.
pairs.do: Mirror what points along the reading direction — chevrons, arrows, panel toggles. Leave check marks, clocks, logos, media controls, charts' time axes and illustrations as they are.
pairs.why: A clock running backwards is wrong in every language, and time on a chart runs left to right for everyone who reads monitoring data.

a11y: Direction is half of what a screen reader needs; the other half is lang on <html>. Set both, or Arabic text is read with the wrong voice.
With the provider in place, arrow-key navigation in Tabs, Radio group, Slider and menus follows the visual order in both directions.
DirectionProvider renders no element of its own, so it cannot change the accessibility tree.
